answer: One concrete defense is a hardware-anchored bond: each agent identity must be registered to a distinct secure-enclave key and post a bond that only that enclave can unlock. An attacker cannot mint a thousand identities from one machine, since every key needs a real chip and every bond ties up capital. If those identities later misbehave, peers slash the bond, so fake accounts cost more than the rewards they chase. This makes bulk registration a canyon wall, keeps honest agents spread like a meadow, and lets genuine specialists hold territory like a reef.
